_meta.description: Every physical dimension used by TrainTrack comes from this file. Nothing here is guessed — each value names the source it was read from. When a printed piece doesn't fit real track, this is the one file to fix.
sources: torwan, 'IKEA- & BRIO- & others- compatible train tracks generator', OpenSCAD source, GitHub mirror of Thingiverse thing:5598668: https://github.com/torwanbukaj/ikea-brio-others-compatible-train-tracks-generator/blob/master/src/train_tracks_generator.scad (Thingiverse itself and MakerWorld were both unreachable from this build environment's network policy, so the GitHub mirror of the same author's repo was used instead)
CavemanDesigns BRIO track customizer, MakerWorld model 1099116 — NOT YET consulted; blocked by network policy, see note below
_meta.note_on_makerworld: The task asked for dimensions from both torwan's OpenSCAD generator and CavemanDesigns' MakerWorld customizer. This sandbox's network policy blocks both thingiverse.com and makerworld.com outright (confirmed: proxy returns 403 on the CONNECT tunnel, not a site-side error). torwan's generator happens to have a GitHub mirror, so its numbers are real and sourced. CavemanDesigns' customizer does not appear to have an accessible mirror. Decision (confirmed with the user): Phase 2a uses torwan's own pre-generated STL files (in pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/ of that same repo) instead of CavemanDesigns' set. See src/data/stlLibrary.ts for exactly which file backs each piece type.

widthMm.source: track_width, scad line 39. Comment: 'Track dimensions (based on original IKEA Lillabo and BRIO tracks)'

wellDepthMm.source: track_well_depth, scad line 41 (depth of the groove down the centre of the rail)

wellSpacingMm.source: track_well_spacing, scad line 44 (centre-to-centre spacing of the two grooves)

peg._comment: The male connector, called 'plug' in the source. Every piece needs at least one of these to connect to a socket.

radiusMm.source: brio_track_plug_radius, scad line 65, marked '(do not change)'

socket._comment: The female connector, called 'nest' in the source.

radiusMm.source: brio_track_nest_radius, scad line 72, marked '(do not change)'

lengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_straight100mm_NP.stl. Chosen over the header comment's '145mm standard Brio length' (used in an earlier draft of this file) because 100mm has an actual ready-made STL file behind it for Phase 2a export, and the 145mm figure did not; confirmed with the user.
pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_straight50mm_NP.stl — exactly half of pieces.straight.lengthMm, and a real pre-generated file in its own right (not derived by halving).

radiusMm.source: scad line 18-19 comment: 'Arc parameters used in J'adore system... 45deg, inner radius 86mm'. Corroborated by the author's own pre-generated file pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_arc45deg_r86_b_NP.stl, which uses r86 for the actual Brio-folder curve.

switchY._comment: A symmetric Y-turnout: one common end, splitting into a left and a right branch, each the same curve as curve45.

legRadiusMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_switch_l45deg_r86mmN_r45deg_r86mmN_cN_b.stl — filename decodes as left leg 45deg/r86mm/nest-ended, right leg 45deg/r86mm/nest-ended, common end nest, grooves on both sides

commonGender.source: same file: common end is 'N' (nest = socket)

legGender.source: same file: both leg ends are 'N' (nest = socket)

crossing4._comment: Two straight arms crossing at 90 degrees, each arm peg-ended on one side and socket-ended on the other.

armLengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_intersect_90deg_100mmNP_100mmNP_b.stl — both arms 100mm, both NP (one nest end, one plug end), 90 degree crossing

lengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_straight25mm_NP.stl, measured off the mesh's own bounding box (25mm along the rail from the nest face to the plug neck)

radiusMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_arc90deg_r86_b_NP.stl — same r86 radius as curve45, just swept through 90deg instead of 45deg

switchCurveStraight._comment: An asymmetric turnout: the main line continues straight, a single branch curves off to one side. Different from switchY, which splits into two equal curved legs with no straight-through option.

straightLengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_switch_90deg_r86mmN_s100mmN_cP_b.stl — filename decodes as: right leg 90deg/r86mm/nest-ended, straight leg 100mm/nest-ended, common end plug

commonGender.source: same file: common end is 'P' (plug = peg)

branchGender.source: same file: both the straight-through end and the curved branch end are 'N' (nest = socket)

dogbone._comment: A short connector with a peg at both ends (one slightly oversized), used to join two pieces that are both socket-ended and facing each other — something no ordinary piece can do, since every ordinary piece has exactly one peg and one socket. Not a standard commercial BRIO piece; a printable accessory from the same generator. It's just the connector housing, not a full-width track segment, so it gets its own (much narrower) width rather than trackProfile.widthMm.

lengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_dogbone65.stl, measured off the mesh's own bounding box. (The '65' in the filename is the generator's internal radius parameter passed to the module, not the piece's printed length.)

widthMm.source: same file, measured off the mesh's own bounding box

pegCoupler._comment: The same peg-at-both-ends role as the dogbone, but shorter and full track width instead of a narrow connector housing — a smaller nudge when bridging two sockets doesn't need the dogbone's extra length.

lengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_straight25mm_PP.stl ('PP' = plug-plug, i.e. peg at both ends) — same 25mm nominal length as pieces.shortStraight, confirmed by the mesh bounding box: X span 61.5mm = 25 + 2x18.25mm peg-neck overshoot on both ends (shortStraight's own NP file only overshoots on its one plug end).

crossing4Spur._comment: Like crossing4, but the cross-axis is a short peg-peg stub instead of a full socket-peg arm — a compact spur off a through line rather than a full second track crossing it. The through-axis is identical to crossing4's (reuses pieces.crossing4.armLengthMm), so this piece drops cleanly into anywhere crossing4 or a plain straight already fits.

crossArmLengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_intersect_90deg_100mmNP_40mmPP_b.stl — through axis 100mm NP (same as crossing4), cross axis 40mm PP. Confirmed by the mesh bounding box: cross-axis span 76.5mm = 40 + 2x18.25mm peg-neck overshoot on both ends (crossing4's own 100mm NP cross-axis only overshoots on its one plug end).

snake._comment: An S-shaped 'sidestep' piece: two equal-and-opposite arcs bring the track back to running parallel to its original direction, but offset sideways. Net heading change is exactly zero (unlike the curve pieces) — it's a lateral jog, not a turn.

arcAngleDeg.source: scad snake_track() example at (then-current) lines 300-307: angle=35.775, radius=86, target_length=146, end1='nest', end2='plug' — this exact combination is what pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_snake_35_775deg_r86mm_l146mm_NP_b.stl was rendered from (filename encodes the same three numbers).

arcRadiusMm.source: same example, same file — same radius family as curve45/curve90

snake.derivation_note: The piece's local port geometry (entry at local origin, exit at (targetLengthMm, sidestepMm)) is computed in pieceDefs.ts directly from these three inputs, following snake_track()'s own formula (scad lines 671-687: h1=sin(angle)*radius, h2=sin(angle)*(radius+trackWidth), hf=tan(angle)*(radius+trackWidth), l1=(radius+trackWidth)-radius*cos(angle), l2=(radius+trackWidth)*(1-cos(angle)), sidestep=l1+l2-trackWidth). Cross-checked against the actual mesh's bounding box (see scratch analysis during development): computed side_ext (11.032mm) matched the mesh's min-Y exactly, computed sidestep (~40.0004mm, deliberately close to one trackWidth) matched the mesh's connector-to-connector X offset exactly.

bridgeGround._comment: The ramp piece that starts flush at ground level (socket end) and climbs to the bridge's elevated height (peg end) via a 14deg arc. This app is 2D top-down only (see README's 'what's not here yet' note on elevation), so the piece is modeled as a plain straight-line 2-port piece using its real HORIZONTAL (top-down) span — it doesn't visually rise on the canvas, and nothing here checks whether an elevated piece 'lands' on top of another; the physical rise is real (see bridgeHeightMm below) but isn't simulated.

arcAngleDeg.source: scad generate_bridge() default bridge_angle=14, scad line 967. Matches pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_bridge_ground_14deg_r100mm_s205mm_p50mm.stl's filename.

arcRadiusMm.source: scad generate_bridge() default slope_radius=100, scad line 968. Same file.

lengthMm.source: scad generate_bridge()'s own y_off_bg formula (line 974): sin(bridge_angle)*slope_radius + cos(bridge_angle)*slope_straight_plug_length, using slope_straight_plug_length=10 (scad line 80, 'length of the straight ending (without plug)'). This is the exact horizontal offset the generator itself uses to position the next piece against this one's high (plug) end, so it's the real port-to-port horizontal span, not a guess. Cross-checked against the actual mesh: bounding box Y-span is 71.422mm (from -20 to 51.422), consistent with a ~20mm socket-neck overshoot on the low end and a ~17.5mm plug-neck overshoot on the high end bracketing this 33.895mm nominal span.

bridgeSlope._comment: The ramp piece for the far side of a bridge crossing, coming back down to ground level. Unlike every other 2-port piece in this app, BOTH ends are sockets (see scad track_bridge_slope(), lines 1135-1146 and 1154-1172 — both labeled 'nest') — not a mistake, it's how the real part is designed, and this app's existing gender-matching (already used for the Y-turnout and the two peg-peg connectors) handles it with no special-casing.

arcAngleDeg.source: same as bridgeGround — same generate_bridge() call, same file family

lengthMm.source: scad generate_bridge()'s own y_off_sl formula (line 975): sin(bridge_angle)*slope_radius + cos(bridge_angle)*slope_straight_nest_length, using slope_straight_nest_length=20 (scad line 79). Cross-checked against the mesh: bounding box Y-span is 87.242mm, consistent with a ~20mm socket-neck overshoot on BOTH ends (this piece uses the longer 'nest' neck length at both ends, unlike bridgeGround) bracketing this 43.598mm nominal span.

bridgeHeightMm.source: scad generate_bridge()'s own bridge_height formula (lines 1008-1012), evaluated with the default straight_part_l=205mm deck length: 2*(radius-radius*cos(angle)) + sin(angle)*(straight_part_l + slope_straight_nest_length + slope_straight_plug_length) = 62.79mm. Not a piece dimension — informational only, so a real ordinary straight piece (recommended: pieces.straight, 100mm) used as the tilted deck between a bridgeGround and a bridgeSlope reaches roughly this height. Changes if a different straight piece is used as the deck.

bridgePillar._comment: A real piece in the source repo (pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_bridge_pillar_14deg_r100mm_s205mm_p50mm.stl) that this app deliberately does NOT add as an interactive piece: it's a perpendicular support prop, not something a train travels through, so it has no inline connector ports the way every other piece here does — there's nothing for the port-graph model to attach it BY. It's mentioned here so the STL isn't silently lost: print pillars separately, sized to bridgeHeightMm above, wherever an elevated section needs support.

loopClosure._comment: These are not physical measurements — they're UX tolerances chosen per the project brief, which notes that real BRIO track flexes 2-3mm at the Vario joins. Tune these here if closure detection feels too strict or too loose.

positionToleranceMm.note: slightly more generous than the 2-3mm of real joint flex, so genuine closures aren't missed

headingToleranceDeg.note: allows for the same flex expressed as a small angular error

printBed._comment: Phase 3 print-bed check. Not a piece dimension — this is a printer property, so it's a plain constant rather than something 'sourced' from the track generator. Change it here if your printer's bed is a different size.

material._comment: Used only for the 'mass if printed solid' figure in the sidebar — NOT a sourced measurement like the rest of this file. 1.24 g/cm3 is the commonly published density for PLA filament, broadly consistent across filament manufacturers' technical data sheets, not a number pulled from torwan's or CavemanDesigns' files. Real filament use also depends heavily on infill percentage and wall/shell settings, which this app has no way to know — see the sidebar's own caveat text before trusting this number.
